script: NBA legends who sacrificed everything for someone else's championship! Shaquille O'Neal had already won four championships by the time the Suns picked him up, but Phoenix never had a real plan for him, and his prime had clearly slipped away. Meanwhile in Cleveland, LeBron James had just watched his Cavaliers get eliminated from the Eastern Conference Finals by Dwight Howard and the Orlando Magic. But Cleveland was about to make a move nobody expected from a team that already won sixty-six games that season. The Cavaliers traded for Shaq, sending Ben Wallace, Sasha Pavlovic, and cash back to Phoenix, and the moment the thirty-seven-year-old arrived in Cleveland, he made his intentions clear. He said his motto was simple: "Win a ring for the king," a direct reference to LeBron, and Shaq spent that season playing a supporting role, hoping to help LeBron win his first championship. But then one moment on the court changed everything. He went up for a shot against the Boston Celtics and severely injured his thumb, requiring surgery. And he recovered just in time for the playoffs. The Cavaliers took down the Chicago Bulls in the first round, then ran into the Celtics again, and this time Cleveland lost in the second round. Shaq never won another ring for the rest of his career.
